title: Backend: fix production-relevant npm audit advisories (body-parser, proxy-addr, qs, zod)
tech: Node/TypeScript backend only -- dependency updates, no feature change
keyConstraints: Found while following up task 037/038's blocked DoD audit gate. IMPORTANT correction to what task 037/038 reports implied ('all advisories are in dev tooling'): that was true for the FRONTEND only. Running `npm audit --omit=dev` in backend/ (i.e. production dependencies only) reports 4 advisories that DO ship: body-parser <1.20.9 HIGH (DoS via trailing bytes after a compressed body), proxy-addr 1.1.0-2.0.7 CRITICAL (IP spoofing via IPv4-mapped IPv6 trust subnet), qs <=6.16.0 MODERATE (array-limit bypass / DoS), and zod <4.6.6 HIGH (memory exhaustion validating oversized constrained collections). body-parser, proxy-addr and qs are transitive dependencies of express ^4.19.2; npm reports `npm audit fix` (non-breaking) resolves all three. zod is a direct dependency pinned ^3.23.8 and npm's only offered fix is `--force` to zod@4.6.7, a MAJOR upgrade -- Architect must NOT run `npm audit fix --force` blindly: first check whether a patched 3.x release exists that resolves the advisory (read the advisory GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5's affected/patched ranges), and if only 4.x is patched, assess the real exposure before deciding to take the major upgrade (every validation schema in backend/src/validation/ uses zod, so a 4.x migration touches request validation across all routes and must be tested accordingly; also zod's own API changes -- e.g. error shape/`issues[0].message` usage seen across the route files -- need checking against the 4.x migration notes). The oversized-collection issue only matters if a schema accepts unbounded arrays from untrusted input -- Architect should check which schemas (if any) validate arrays and whether those already have .max() limits, which may reduce real exposure and inform the decision. Related thing to CHECK (not assume): backend/src/app.ts never sets `trust proxy`, and the rate limiters in backend/src/middleware/rateLimit.ts use express-rate-limit's default req.ip. The app runs behind Railway's proxy, so without `trust proxy` req.ip may be the proxy's address for every customer (all users sharing one rate-limit bucket) -- while enabling it incorrectly would instead make the proxy-addr spoofing advisory directly exploitable (clients could forge X-Forwarded-For to dodge rate limits). Architect should determine what express/express-rate-limit actually do in production here and report; if a change is warranted it is a decision for Ville, not part of silently fixing this task. Remaining backend advisories are dev-toolchain only (vitest ^2 -> tinypool CRITICAL and @vitest/mocker, esbuild, minimatch, brace-expansion, source-map-js) and arrive via vitest/vite; `npm audit fix` handles the non-breaking ones, tinypool/@vitest/mocker/esbuild need `--force` (vitest major upgrade). Treat the dev-tooling vitest major upgrade as optional within this task: do the production fixes first and independently verifiable; take the vitest upgrade only if the full backend suite (229+ tests, integration tests need the test database) passes unchanged, otherwise leave it and document. Keep lockfile changes minimal and reviewable -- list exactly which packages changed version.
description: Resolve the npm audit advisories in the backend's production dependencies (body-parser, proxy-addr, qs, zod), including one CRITICAL and two HIGH, so the DoD audit gate can pass for backend work, and report on whether the proxy/rate-limiting setup is correct in production.
acceptanceCriteria: `npm audit --omit=dev` in backend/ reports no HIGH or CRITICAL advisories (document precisely what was done for zod, including the reasoning if a major upgrade is taken or deliberately deferred with a written risk assessment)
Express-transitive fixes (body-parser, proxy-addr, qs) applied via a non-breaking update; resulting package versions listed in the report

If zod is upgraded to 4.x: every validation schema and every use of parsed.error.issues[0].message still behaves identically, covered by tests, with the migration notes consulted; if not upgraded: the unbounded-array exposure assessment is documented

Written finding on `trust proxy` / rate-limit client identification behind Railway (what req.ip is in production, whether limits are per-client or shared, and whether a change is recommended) -- no behaviour change to rate limiting without Ville's explicit decision
Full backend test suite passes unchanged (unit + integration), build, lint and tsc --noEmit pass
Lockfile diff is limited to the intended packages; no new direct dependency added
securityConsiderations: This task exists for security reasons: it addresses a CRITICAL IP-spoofing advisory and HIGH DoS advisories in production dependencies. SECURITY stage should verify the production audit is clean afterwards and scrutinise the rate-limiting/trust-proxy finding, since a wrong trust-proxy setting can either collapse all clients into one bucket or let clients spoof their IP.
